title: Kawaiisu language - Wikipedia
text: Kawaiisu is a member of the Southern Numic division of the Uto-Aztecan language family. The Kawaiisu homeland was bordered by speakers of non-Numic Uto-Aztecan languages: the Kitanemuk to the south spoke Takic, the Tubatulabal to the north spoke Tubatulabal, the Yokuts to the west were non-Uto-Aztecan.

title: Kawaiisu - Wikipedia
text: They were divided into two regional groups: the "Desert Kawaiisu" and the "Mountain Kawaiisu". The Kawaiisu are related by language and culture to the Southern Paiute of southwestern Nevada and the Chemehuevi of the eastern Mojave Desert of California.

title: Kawaiisu - California Language Archive
text: Kawaiisu is a member of the Numic branch of the Uto-Aztecan language family. Within Numic, it is most closely related to Chemehuevi -Southern Paiute-Ute, spoken in southeastern California and throughout Nevada, Utah, Colorado, and Arizona.

title: Kawaiisu language, alphabet and pronunciation - Omniglot
text: Kawaiisu is a member of the Southern Numic division of the Uto-Aztecan language family. It was traditionally spoken in the Tehachapi and Piute mountains in the southern Sierra Nevada in California.

title: Kawaiisu Language - YouTube
text: Feb 26, 2018 · Kawaiisu is a Uto-Aztecan language that is currently critically endangered. With only three native speakers at the moment, linguists are working to preserve and save the Kawaiisu language.

title: Kawaiisu language
text: The Kawaiisu language is a critically endangered member of the Southern Numic branch of the Uto-Aztecan language family, traditionally spoken by the Kawaiisu people in the southern Sierra Nevada region of California, including the Tehachapi and Piute Mountains.

title: Kawaiisu Language (XAW) – L1 & L2 Speakers... | Ethnologue Free
text: Kawaiisu is an endangered indigenous language of the United States. It belongs to the Uto-Aztecan language family. The language is used as a first language by the elderly only. It is not known to be taught in schools.
